comparison_scope: common feed IDs only; statuses, validator findings and timing. Both runs captured wall time for every completed state, so timing is comparable.
note: The catalog did not move: 4,271 feeds in both runs, none added or removed. Two feeds changed status. mdb-2014 is a measurement correction rather than a change in the data: byte-identical across both runs and killed by timeout at 300 s in both, it was recorded as analyzer_state=completed with 1,551,740 notices in run 32145833613 because classify_analyzer never read the exit code. It now reads timeout with zero, and MobilityData also moved from partial_internal to timeout on it, so neither validator finishes that feed. The entire -1,552,201 drop in Analyzer findings is that single feed leaving the totals; the real product change over the corpus is -461. The second change is mdb-2250, where MobilityData went from completed to partial_internal on our side of an unchanged Analyzer state - a movement on their side, not ours.
